sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Appling County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Two offices in the Courthouse Annex at 69 Tippins Street in Baxley split the work: the Board of Tax Assessors sets the value and the Tax Commissioner sends and collects the bill. Property owners often call the wrong one first, so it helps to know which questions go where.

The assessors answer questions about your appraised value, property record errors, exemptions and appeals. The tax commissioner answers questions about what you owe, how to pay and what happens when a bill goes unpaid. Appling County posts its property records at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the tax commissioner's page lists a county payment portal for online payments.

sections.h2: What is Appling County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Appling County is a rural county of about 507 square miles of land in southeast Georgia, with Baxley as the county seat and the largest town. Graham and Surrency are the other municipalities, and Holmesville, the old county seat before the railroad shifted things in 1872, is now an unincorporated community.

The Census Bureau counts 19,100 residents for July 2025, which works out to roughly 36 people per square mile. Homeowners make up 72.5 percent of households, and the median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $76,700. Median household income over the same period is $46,651. Those figures describe a county where homes are modest in price, so even a few years of unpaid tax can be a meaningful part of what a house will sell for.

  • The Altamaha River drains the northern third of the county, and the southern two-thirds sits in the Little Satilla River sub-basin, so a parcel's water drainage depends on which basin it falls in.
  • The Edwin I. Hatch nuclear plant north of Baxley on U.S. 1 is the area's largest employer, and a sawmill adds jobs in town.
  • Appling County School District runs elementary schools, a middle school and a high school for the whole county.
  • Neighboring counties are Toombs, Tattnall, Wayne, Pierce, Jeff Davis and Bacon.

Baxley grew up around a Macon and Brunswick Railroad depot in 1870 and incorporated in 1875.

sections.h2: How does Appling County value a house for tax?
sections.html:
The Board of Tax Assessors sets fair market value as of January 1 each year, and the taxable assessment is 40 percent of that value. Georgia's revenue department describes the bill as the assessed value, minus any exemption, multiplied by the millage rate, where one mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

Appling's assessors tell owners that returns are filed with their office between January 1 and April 1, and that a new return is needed only when property is added or changed. Skipping a required return carries a 10 percent penalty on the value that went unreturned, plus interest. Personal property returns, such as business equipment, are filed with the same office every year by April 1.

Assessment notices go out in the spring. The county's assessor page says they arrive in May and carry an estimated bill based on the prior year's millage rates. That estimate is not something to pay. Neither the county nor the school board has adopted a budget at that stage, and the real rates are typically set around September.

sections.h2: When is Appling County property tax due?
sections.html:
Georgia's revenue department says taxes are normally due December 20 in most counties, with 60 days from the billing date to pay. Appling County's own due date is printed on your bill, so read the bill itself or call the tax commissioner at (912) 367-8105 before relying on any calendar.

Bills are mailed to the owner of record on January 1, even if the house has since been sold. That is the detail that trips up sellers. If you sell in June, the county still bills the person who owned the property on January 1, and the closing paperwork decides who really pays.

  • Taxes are paid at the tax commissioner's office, by mail, or through the county's online payment page.
  • Ask the office for a payoff figure in writing before closing if any prior year is unpaid.
  • Mobile homes follow separate rules: owners apply to the tax commissioner for a location permit within 30 days of placing the home and renew it each year between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Appling County assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Appling County Board of Tax Assessors, Suite 101 at 69 Tippins Street, within 45 days of the date printed on your notice. The appeal can cover taxability, value or uniformity, and it cannot be based on a complaint about the tax rate.

The state's uniform form is the PT-311A, and it asks you to choose a path at the start. If the assessors keep the value, the file moves to the county Board of Equalization, a panel appointed by the grand jury. Arbitration is the alternative, and a hearing officer is available only for non-homestead real property valued above $500,000. A Superior Court appeal needs a written notice filed with the assessors within 30 days of the decision, and the taxes owed must be paid before a court hears the case.

The 45-day window is strict. Appling's assessors say plainly that appeals must reach their office by the deadline on the notice, and the Department of Revenue says it cannot override local boards on an individual appraisal.

sections.h2: What homestead exemption can an Appling County owner claim?
sections.html:
Owners who live in their house as a primary residence can claim the standard homestead exemption, and Appling County has raised the amounts above the state minimum. In Appling the exemption application is filed with the Tax Assessors' office, not the tax commissioner.

The application can be filed in the year the home becomes your primary residence, up to and including April 1 of the following year. Once granted, it renews automatically unless you want a different type. Because the exemption attaches to the owner, a buyer who moves in must file their own. Sellers sometimes forget that the exemption on their current bill disappears after the sale and the next owner starts without it.

Ask the assessors for the current local amounts. The county's tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category, and the Board of Commissioners also posts a notice about a school district ad valorem exemption on its meetings page.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Appling County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, so an unpaid balance has to be cleared at or before closing. Georgia law makes the person who owned the property on January 1 responsible for that year's bill, and the state revenue department confirms there is no refund for a partial year of ownership.

In practice, the seller and buyer divide the year in the purchase contract, and the closing attorney pays the county from the proceeds. If a delinquent balance has become a recorded lien, it sits in the clerk's records and has to be satisfied before the buyer gets clean title.

  • Get a payoff statement from the tax commissioner for every open year.
  • Check the Clerk of Courts records for liens on the parcel.
  • If the house belongs to an estate, the Probate Court on South Main Street in Baxley is where estate administration is handled.
  • Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork with the closing file.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Appling County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Tax Commissioner's office, 69 Tippins Street, Suite 102 in Baxley, by mail, or through the county's online payment page. The office phone is (912) 367-8105 and it lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What share of market value is taxed in Appling County?
faqs.a: Forty percent. Georgia assesses property at 40 percent of fair market value, and Appling's assessors apply that ratio to a January 1 value. Exemptions come off the assessed figure before the millage rate is applied.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal if my notice arrived in May and I missed the window?
faqs.a: No. The 45-day window runs from the date on the notice, and Appling's assessors say an appeal cannot be filed after that period. For the next year, mark the deadline the day the notice arrives and call (912) 367-8108 with any questions.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller pay the tax bill in the year of sale?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 is billed, but the contract can shift the cost between buyer and seller. The closing attorney normally prorates the year and pays the county at closing, so confirm that the settlement statement shows the bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the value of my Appling County house?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Tax Assessors at (912) 367-8108. The assessors maintain property records, take appeals and handle exemption applications. Billing and payment questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105.
